newsitem.title: ITALY: League dissident sees Islam in Italy's south.
newsitem.headline: League dissident sees Islam in Italy's south.

text.p: A prominent critic of the Northern League party's campaign for independence in Italy's north suggested on Tuesday that a such a division would expose the poorer south to an Islamic "threat".

Irene Pivetti, a former speaker of Italy's lower house of parliament, is a member of the League but has broken with firebrand leader Umberto Bossi over his plans to proclaim a self-styled northern republic he calls Padania on September 15.

Pivetti, a fundamentalist Roman Catholic, wrote in the weekly magazine Tempi that a breakaway by the affluent north would expose the historically less-developed south of Italy not only to more organised crime and poverty.
She said that, with a north transformed "into a new Bavaria, the south would plunge to the economic level of the Maghreb".

"There is no doubt that the frontiers of Islam would immediately shift from the shores of Africa to those of our peninsula though an acceleration of the migratory flow and a diminished ability to control the borders," she wrote.

Pivetti raised eyebrows in June last year when, while still Speaker, she joined a prayer recital in a church in Rome organised by arch-conservative Catholics to display dismay at the opening of the city's first mosque.
While she insisted she was there in a personal capacity, critics said her presence could be construed as a sign of religious intolerance from a senior representative of the state.
